 TSMC Stocks Move Lower as November Sales Data Face a $53.3 Billion Quarterly Hurdle
 Khac Phu Nguyen Wed, November 4, 2026 at 9:15 AM CST 1 min read TSM -7.66%

 TSMC ( NYSE:TSM ), the Taiwanese chip manufacturer, rose 0.26% to $405.87 at 9:41 a.m. ET on November 4 as investors looked toward its next revenue test. The company's financial calendar lists October sales for November 10 at 1:30 p.m. Taipei time, although the schedule remains subject to change. That release could offer an early read on whether its fourth-quarter growth ambitions are taking shape. 
 Warning! GuruFocus has detected 2 Warning Sign with QCOM. 
 Is TSM fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator. 
 TSM GF Value chart Management set a demanding target in its October 15 presentation: fourth-quarter revenue of $52.3 billion to $54.3 billion, following approximately $46.7 billion in the preceding quarter. Gross margin is projected at 65% to 67%, with operating margin of 56.5% to 58.5%, under its stated exchange-rate assumption. The $53.3 billion revenue midpoint implies roughly 14.1% sequential growtha substantial step up that puts the coming monthly sales figures under closer scrutiny. 
 Reaching that midpoint would require average monthly revenue of about $17.77 billion, although that calculation is a yardstick rather than an October forecast. Monthly sales arrive in Taiwan dollars, so investors need comparable exchange rates before measuring progress. The ten-year chart shows a gain of roughly 1,191% alongside a retreat of about 16.7% from its high, illustrating how a powerful long-term advance can still carry sharp pullbacks. October sales could help test the growth case, but revenue alone cannot establish whether product mix and margins will meet management's targets.
